chunk_findings.detail: This function documents and is meant to accept a detached worktree during “a rebase in progress” by testing that `branch` is an ancestor of `HEAD`, but that commit check is false for the normal Git rebase state. During a rebase, `refs/heads/{branch}` still points at the pre-rebase tip while the worktree is detached at the newly rewritten commits; the old tip is not an ancestor of the new rebased HEAD. For example, item `feature` has recorded worktree `/repo/.ddflow/worktrees/f`, and a rebase stops at a conflict there. `_is_items_tree(repo, path, "feature")` then runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/heads/feature HEAD`, which exits nonzero, so `_is_items_tree` returns `False` and `_recorded_tree` returns `None`. A re-claim during an interrupted rebase therefore fails to re-bind to the item’s recorded worktree, which is the exact orphaning this code is supposed to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: `_SENTENCE_END.finditer(text, 0, room)` stops at index `room`, so a sentence whose period/semicolon is the last character inside `room` is not matched because the following whitespace is at index `room` and is outside `endpos`. For example, `text = "A " + "B"*113 + ". " + "C"*200` has length > 120 and `room == 116`; the period is at index 115, followed by the space at index 116. `finditer(..., 0, 116)` returns no sentence-end match, so `_listed` falls back to `text[:116].rsplit(" ", 1)[0]`, which is `"A"`. It therefore returns `"A ..."` even though the available sentence boundary would allow the advertised help to keep the much fuller `"A " + "B"*113 + ". ..."`. The function claims to cut at the last sentence end that fits, but the off-by-one `endpos` misses the boundary case.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `full.startswith(listed.removesuffix(FS.CUT_MARK))` does not require `listed` to actually contain `FS.CUT_MARK`. chunk_findings.detail: `_is_items_tree` claims to recognize “a rebase in progress” as the item’s own detached tree, but the check `git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/heads/{branch} HEAD` is normally false during an actual rebase. In a rebase/conflict, the branch ref still points at the original tip while HEAD is detached at a new/cherry-picked commit, so the original branch is not an ancestor of HEAD. For an item whose worktree is mid-rebase, `_recorded_tree` therefore returns `None`, and a re-claim will not bind to that tree; `merge` can then merge an empty branch and orphan the salvage.

data.summary: _lock_wait gives the queue wait the whole per-run timeout and the run behind it gets the same budget again, so `ddflow ci run --timeout N` can take 2N seconds. Observed 2026-11-05: a --full run with timeout 7200 in an agent's background shell queued from 23:36 to 01:36, reached #1 in the queue, and was killed at the harness's 7200 s limit having run no test. Expected: one overall deadline for wait plus run, or a durable queued run that outlives its launcher (as `review --detach` does).

chunk_findings.detail: The new early return trusts `it.merged_head` (or a merged PR head) as proof that the branch is currently merged, without checking whether the current `base` still contains the recorded landing. Input: `feature` is squash-merged into `main`, recording `merged_head = F`; `main` is then force-pushed back to its pre-merge commit, while `feature` remains at `F`. `ddflow complete feature` reaches this line, sees `W.rev(repo, "feature") == F` in `landed`, and returns `[]`, skipping the real `W.is_merged(repo, "feature", "main")` check. That allows completion and silently drops commits from a base that no longer has them, exactly the partial-landing case this guard exists to prevent. The added test only covers a commit added after a recorded landing, not the recorded landing being undone on the base.

chunk_findings.detail: The new early return trusts `it.merged_head` (or a merged PR head) as proof that the branch is currently merged, without checking whether the current `base` still contains the recorded landing. Input: `feature` is squash-merged into `main`, recording `merged_head = F`; `main` is then force-pushed back to its pre-merge commit, while `feature` remains at `F`. `ddflow complete feature` reaches this line, sees `W.rev(repo, "feature") == F` in `landed`, and returns `[]`, skipping the real `W.is_merged(repo, "feature", "main")` check. That allows completion and silently drops commits from a base that no longer has them, exactly the partial-landing case this guard exists to prevent. The added test only covers a commit added after a recorded landing, not the recorded landing being undone on the base.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous review’s “or a merged PR head” case is still present, just moved. The new line `if it.pr and it.pr.state == "merged" and tip == it.pr.head_sha: return []` trusts the PR head as proof the work is currently merged, with no `W.is_merged(repo, it.merged_sha, base)` check even when `it.merged_sha` is available. chunk_findings.detail: The change still does not fix the PR-request half of B-unmerged-guard-breaks-pr-and-squash. It only bypasses `UNMERGED_BLOCKER` when `it.pr.state == "merged"`. W.is_merged(repo, it.merged_sha, base)` guard protects the `merged_head` path, but the merged-PR-head path still returns `[]` on the forge's word without verifying that the current `base` contains the PR's landing. Concrete failure: a `feature` branch is squash-merged via a PR, so `it.pr.state == "merged"` and `it.pr.head_sha == feature`'s tip. Input: `feature` is squash-merged via PR into `main`; the record has `pr.state="merged"`, `pr.head_sha=F`, `merged_sha=S`; then `main` is force-pushed back to its pre-merge commit while `feature` remains at `F`. `W.is_merged(repo, "feature", "main")` is false and `tip = F == it.pr.head_sha`, so the PR-merged passthrough returns `[]` before the repaired `merged_sha` check. chunk_findings.detail: The squash-landing passthrough only accepts the exact recorded `merged_sha` as merged into base. Input: `feature` at `F` is squash-merged to `main` as `S`, so `merged_sha=S`, `merged_head=F`; later `main` is rebased so `S` is rewritten as `S'` with the same patch.
